rule: Each plan case of the group, in plan order. Every case waits for W06's enrolled AMD64 and ARM64 hosts and is NOT_RUN_ENV_UNAVAILABLE until W06 runs it, never PASS before (AGENTS rule 14); D-PROBE-ROUTE (owner decision Q-T14) gates that run too, and `permissions` lists, in SELinux matrix v4 terms, what the case's probe needs beyond an enrolled host's policy. Its catalog names the contract rows (with the file each comes from) whose expected results W06 checks with the reference models while the case's probe runs. `probe` names the probe crate and case that inject the native fault, or `probeIn` the packet that brings them; a case with neither is judged by its catalog rows only. `verdicts` names the checks that judge the probe's timeline with W06's answer log, and `carries` the LEDGER-E09 properties the case carries (owner decision Q-T11) with the checks that observe each. In W06 a case is PASS only when its probe's faultResult is PASS in every run the case needs (one per peer for peer death/restart) and every verdict, catalog-row and carried-property check is PASS; it is FAIL when any of them fails, and NOT_RUN_ENV_UNAVAILABLE otherwise. A catalog row is checked in W06 when it is a vector (replayed through its reference model against the run's records) or a model rule (applied to the run's captures); spec-step and obligation rows are the basis the verdict and vector checks cite, not checks of their own. `harnessRestore` is what W06's harness does after every run, whether or not the probe ended.
